$comment: Vector layer definitions. The map, the layer toggles, the legends and the tile routes all read this. Adding a layer means adding an entry here plus a PostGIS MVT function, not editing a component. Fields listed under properties are the ones popups and labels may reference, and their names must match the database columns exactly because they are join keys.
$colorPolicy: Every layer owns one distinct hue, declared once in `color` and used for the fill, the outline and the legend swatch. One value means the legend can never drift from the map. Hues are spaced around the wheel so no two layers read alike on satellite imagery, where everything competes with the ground. These are data identity colours, not theme colours, so they are identical in light and dark, exactly like the risk palettes.

legend.description: Country outline, disputed territory shown separately

layers.label: Districts
layers.$comment: joinKey is district_code, not district_name. Poonch exists on both sides of the Line of Control, so the name identifies a district only within its province.

legend.description: 188 districts, the unit every model scores

layers.label: Tehsils
layers.$comment: district_src is the district name as the tehsil file spells it, which predates the 2018 district changes. district_code is the reconciled parent and is what to join on.
layers.$minzoomNote: 0, not 6. A minzoom of 6 sat above the default view zoom of 4.6, so switching the layer on did nothing and it read as broken. The gateway enforces minzoom too, so it was returning 204 for the tiles the map wanted. At national zoom the whole layer is 108 KB and 34k vertices, well inside the 65k Mapbox bucket limit, so there was nothing to protect against.

legend.description: 553 tehsils, boundaries predate the 2018 district changes

layers.label: IIOJK Districts
layers.$comment: Not a separate table. The delivered district layer carries all 22 disputed districts with real names under province_code IJK, so this is geo.districts filtered. Kept as its own layer so the map can style and toggle it separately. Always scores against the terrain matrix.
